Subject: Post-demo: encryption / KMS follow-up + next steps

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap on the encryption and data controls we discussed and proposed next steps so your security team can validate fit: 

1) In-transit encryption
- All network traffic to/from Redwood is TLS 1.2+ (we recommend 1.3 where supported).

2) At-rest encryption
- Default: data encrypted at-rest using provider-managed keys (AES-256).
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK): supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Private (VPC or on-prem) we can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or an HSM-backed key provider.

3) Key management / HSM options
- Dedicated: Option to use customer-managed keys via a vault in your cloud account (envelope encryption).
- Private/on-prem: full KMS/HSM integration (FIPS 140-2 HSMs supported).
- Hosted (shared): we currently encrypt at-rest with strong provider keys; for enterprise customers we support a bring-your-own-key model only for Dedicated/Private.

4) Key rotation and export
- We support automated rotation schedules and manual rotation. Keys used for envelope encryption are not exportable from your KMS/HSM.

5) Logging / audit / retention
- Audit logs: request-level logs (metadata + routing) available.
- Customer audit log retention configurable on Dedicated/Private. For hosted accounts we can provide log exports and S3/Cloud Storage delivery for agreed retention windows.
- PII handling: we offer optional redaction and configurable retention policies per route.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send our KMS one-pager and architecture doc (attached).
- If helpful, schedule a 30-min security sync with our infra/security engineer (David).
- Please share the security questionnaire and point person from your team.

Attachments: redwood-kms-overview.pdf (overview), redwood-kms-architecture.pdf (deployment diagrams)

Thanks — happy to walk through any of the items in more detail.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Tom —

Great questions, answered inline below.

> Can you confirm whether BYOK is available for the hosted (shared) offering at all, or is it strictly Dedicated/Private?

Short answer: BYOK (customer-managed KMS keys) is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For our hosted shared offering we do not currently support full customer-managed keys that isolate encryption at-rest per customer; however we provide robust envelope encryption and can arrange log export / encrypted backups to your storage for compliance purposes in the hosted offering. If BYOK is a hard requirement the recommended path is Dedicated or Private.

> Regarding HSM: do you offer HSM-backed keys (e.g., AWS CloudHSM) for Dedicated, or is HSM only for Private/on-prem installs?

We support HSM-backed keys in Private deployments (on-prem or VPC-connected where the customer controls the HSM). For Dedicated we can integrate with cloud HSM services (CloudHSM, KMS with HSM-backed key material) depending on the cloud provider and contract. We'll surface the exact options in the security call.

> For retention: we generally need 90-day audit logs and a 30-day data retention window for request-level data, with an option to extend backups for compliance. Can Redwood export audit logs to our S3/Cloud Storage?

Yes — for Dedicated and Private, audit logs and raw request logs can be exported to your storage bucket (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) with configurable retention (90 days or as agreed). For hosted customers we can arrange periodic exports and API access to logs, but retention beyond default windows is handled via exports.

Next steps:
- I'll loop David (infra/security) to run through KMS policies and rotation requirements in a short call.
- Please send over your security questionnaire and the contact for your cloud/KMS admin.
- I'll attach our KMS architecture diagram and a short FAQ.

Proposed times for a 30-min security sync: Tue 6/16 11:00am PT or Wed 6/17 2:00pm PT — which works for you?

Thanks,
Marissa
